Ui.Script:
-- The reference's own body, captured before we shadow the name. Nil on a machine with no -- client data (nothing was sourced) — which must be LOUD at the call, not a quiet no-op: -- a bag hover that silently does nothing is precisely the failure mode that let Bagnon -- ship "working" through four green survey columns. local refItemButtonOnEnter = ContainerFrameItemButton_OnEnter
function ContainerFrameItemButton_OnEnter(button) if not button then button = this end if not button then return end
-- benilla's keyring is a CONTAINER (0765), so the reference's inventory-slot detour is -- both unavailable and wrong here; this is the same pair of calls its general path -- makes for every other bag, which is all a keyring slot ever needed. if button:GetParent():GetID() == KEYRING_CONTAINER then if (button:GetRight() or 0) >= (GetScreenWidth() / 2) then GameTooltip:SetOwner(button, "ANCHOR_LEFT") else GameTooltip:SetOwner(button, "ANCHOR_RIGHT") end GameTooltip:SetBagItem(KEYRING_CONTAINER, button:GetID()) ResetCursor() return end
if not refItemButtonOnEnter then message("benilla: Interface\\FrameXML\\ContainerFrame.lua was not sourced from the " .. "game data, so bag-slot tooltips cannot work. Check the client data path.") return end refItemButtonOnEnter(button) end
-- ══ Re-publishing the three bag verbs 0561 shadows, and why it is HERE ═════════════ -- -- `OpenBackpack`, `CloseBackpack` and `CloseAllBags` are all defined by the sourced -- `ContainerFrame.lua` (l.187-217, l.702-707) — and benilla answers all three differently, -- for one reason: **0561, the director's call that a window opening your bags opens EVERY -- equipped bag**, not just the backpack. The vendor, bank, mail and trade windows call -- `OpenBackpack` from their OnShow so your bags come up with them and you can sell or -- deposit from one. -- -- The bodies live in `UiPanels.xml`, because every window that calls them is loaded by -- harnesses that have no bag stack at all, and a nil `OpenBackpack` in a merchant test is -- a nil for no reason. But UiPanels is manifest entry 7 and the reference's container file -- is entry 46, so **its publications lose the collision** — the reference's bodies land on -- top and the vendor silently stops opening your bags. That is not hypothetical: it is -- what shipped for the length of one session before a test caught it. -- -- So the bodies stay where their callers can reach them, under `Benilla*` names that -- nothing overwrites, and this file — entry 49, after the reference's — puts them back on -- the reference's names. Three lines, and they are the whole of the fix. OpenBackpack = BenillaOpenBackpack CloseBackpack = BenillaCloseBackpack CloseAllBags = BenillaCloseAllBags
-- ══ THE ITEM-PUSH DROP CARD, over the reference's own bag bar (decision 0887) ═════════ -- -- The bar is `Interface\FrameXML\MainMenuBarBagButtons.xml` now (1751 window 3), and its -- `ItemAnimTemplate` is a `<Model>` playing `Interface\ItemAnimations\ForcedBackpackItem.mdx`. -- **This engine's `<Model>` holds the scene the Lua API reads and writes but draws no -- pixels** (`script/modelframe.rs` — the pane is the app renderer's job and no renderer -- claims a FrameXML model), so those six frames load, register, and animate nothing. -- -- That is a genuine engine difference, which is the one thing 1751 §2 keeps an adapter -- for. So the reference's file is sourced unedited — its Models exist and are harmless — -- and the card the player actually sees is built HERE, as a sibling Frame + Texture on the -- same six buttons, driven by the model's OWN keyframes read out of the shipped .m2. The -- bodies below moved verbatim from the deleted `BagFrame.xml`; every number in them is -- byte-derived and the comments carry their provenance. -- -- ONE THING CHANGED IN THE MOVE, and it is the reason the swap needed thought at all. -- `ItemAnim_OnEvent` matches on `this:GetParent():GetID()`, which for a bag button is its -- INVENTORY-slot id (20..23, via `GetInventorySlotInfo`). benilla used to translate -- `ITEM_PUSH`'s `arg1` into its own container vocabulary (1..4) because the old bar was -- keyed that way, and against the reference's body that comparison is false for every bag -- — four cards that would simply never have played, with nothing raising. The fix was not -- to adapt the reference: `ui_loot.rs`'s `push_container` stopped translating and now emits -- `0x491bb5`'s selector verbatim, which is what addons expect too. So the id a card matches -- on is `button:GetID()`, exactly as the reference's own body reads it. -- ── The item-push drop animation (decision 0887) ───────────────────────────────────────── -- An item lands in a bag: its icon pops in above the bag bar, hangs there, then falls into -- the button that took it and shrinks away. ref ItemAnim (MainMenuBarBagButtons.xml l.4-16 + -- .lua l.68-80, .lua l.92-94): each bag button owns a hidden child that, on ITEM_PUSH -- naming its own container, swaps in the pushed item's icon, rewinds to sequence time 0 and -- shows itself; OnAnimFinished hides it again. A second push on the same button RESTARTS it -- (SetSequenceTime(0,0)); pushes into different bags run independently. That is exactly the -- machine below, with the reference's ITEM_PUSH `arg1` translated from its inventory-slot -- vocabulary (20..23) into ours (bagId 1..4) app-side — ui_loot.rs `push_container` carries -- the byte-verified selector. -- -- The reference's is a <Model> playing Interface\ItemAnimations\ForcedBackpackItem.mdx — a -- single 4-vertex quad on one animated bone, i.e. a 2D icon card with keyframed scale, alpha -- and offset. benilla has no Model widget (decision 0137's Cooldown took the same posture: -- model the mechanism, let our own renderer draw it), so it is a Texture driven by the -- model's OWN tracks, read out of the shipped .m2 with `benilla-extract m2anim`/`m2bones`: -- -- sequence 0, CLAMP (plays once), duration 1.000 s -- texture-weight (alpha) 0.000→0.0 0.133→1.0 0.267→1.0 1.000→0.0 linear -- bone 0 scale 0.000→1.0 0.133→1.2 0.267→1.0 1.000→0.014 linear -- bone 0 translation 0.000→(0,0) 0.500→(0,0) 1.000→(+0.010,-0.040) -- the quad itself: 0.03 x 0.03 model units, blend Alpha, unlit, no depth write -- -- So: fade in over the first 133 ms while swelling to 1.2x; settle back to full size by -- 267 ms; from there dwindle and fade continuously for the remaining 733 ms — while the -- POSITION holds until the half-second and only then falls. The three tracks deliberately -- do not share a schedule: the card is already down to ~0.69 size and ~0.68 alpha when it -- starts moving, so the drop reads as the icon being drawn into the bag rather than as a -- solid tile sliding. Those numbers are the file's, not ours. -- -- THE MODEL-UNIT → PIXEL SCALE is no longer ours to calibrate: the <Model> widget's -- projection is RE-recorded now (wow-re `system/ui/scratch/modelframe-animation-clock.md`, -- dispatched over the pet bar's B228 and folded back with it). The ortho leg gives -- -- px per model unit = (5/3) * modelScale * layoutScale * screenHeightPx -- -- which in FrameXML units is **1280 * modelScale * layoutScale**, aspect- and -- resolution-independent, with the model ORIGIN at the frame rect's bottom-left. The ref's -- `ItemAnimTemplate` (MainMenuBarBagButtons.xml:4) carries **no `scale` attribute**, so -- modelScale is 1 and the constant is a flat 1280. Decision 0887's named gap is closed. -- -- This REPLACES a back-fit, and the back-fit is worth naming because it looked like -- evidence. The old 1200 came from assuming CooldownFrameTemplate's 0.04-unit sweep -- *exactly* covers a 36 px action button at its scale="0.75" (⇒ K = 1200). The assumption -- is the error: at the real projection that sweep is 0.04 · 1280 · 0.75 = **38.4 px**, so -- it overhangs its button by 6.7% rather than fitting it — exactly as the autocast shine's -- 30.72 px square overhangs its 30 px button. Solving against a wrong premise produced a -- number that then "cross-checked" against a second model derived the same wrong way, and -- both files cited the agreement as the reason to trust it. -- -- Everything below is the model's own ratios times this constant, so the correction lands -- in one place and the animation stays in proportion. BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_PX_PER_UNIT = 1280 BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_DURATION = 1.0
-- ── The widget rect, and why the card is not placed against the button ───────────────── -- A `<Model>` with no `<Size>` and no `setAllPoints` takes its rect from the **M2 header -- bounding box** (`MD20+0xB4`, max−min per axis), consumed RAW as layout units — unlike -- CSimpleTexture's texel fallback, there is no AbsDimension conversion. So the ref's -- ItemAnim widget is **42.41 x 124.72**, nothing like the 36-square everyone assumes from -- looking at the XML, and **model-space (0,0,0) lands on that rect's BOTTOM-LEFT corner**. -- (wow-re `system/ui/scratch/modelframe-implicit-size-law.md`, §5-cross-checked: vtable -- 0x81c5d8 +0x1c/+0x20 -> 0x76d080/0x76d0d0, bbox source 0x713640 at `713661 add esi,0xb4`. -- The one worker who read `MD20+0xD0` — the VertexBox — got an all-zero box and concluded -- the widget was degenerate; that wrong premise is exactly what the pair round exists to -- catch, and it is why this looked unresolvable in 0887.) -- -- That rect is the whole reason this animation reads the way it does: it stands 124.72 tall -- off the button's own bottom edge, so the card's travel band reaches **54 px above the -- button's top**. Decision 0887 could not know that and placed the card against the -- button's CENTER instead, which is what put it in the wrong place in x and gave it no -- horizontal drift at all. BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_FRAME_W = 42.41 BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_FRAME_H = 124.72 -- Where that rect hangs off the button: the ref anchors the widget's BOTTOMRIGHT to the -- button's, 10 in from the right for the five bag buttons and flush (0) for the keyring — -- MainMenuBarBagButtons.xml l.19-27 (BagSlotButtonTemplate) and l.152-160 (KeyRingButton). -- Per-button, so it is an OnLoad argument, not a constant. BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_ANCHOR_X = -10
-- ── The model's own numbers, unrounded ──────────────────────────────────────────────── -- Every one of these was rounded in 0887 and every rounding moved the card. The quad span -- read as 0.03 (it is 0.0288 — a 4% size error), and the translation as (0.010, -0.040) -- (which alone accounts for half a pixel of the landing point). -- -- The bone transform is `v' = pivot + T(t) + S(t) * (v - pivot)` — three wow-re workers -- derived that independently in three matrix conventions and agreed. The pivot -- (M2CompBone+0x60) is NOT the quad's centre: it sits 0.23 px right and 0.07 px above it, -- so the card shrinks *almost* in place and drifts a fifth of a pixel doing it. Keeping -- the pivot as its own term rather than folding it into the centre is what makes this -- reproduce the reference exactly at all three sampled times instead of nearly. -- Bone 0's ROTATION track is empty (nKeys = 0), so there is no roll to model. BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_PIVOT_X = 0.017580900341272354 BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_PIVOT_Y = 0.053958501666784286 BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_QUAD_X = 0.017400000942870975 BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_QUAD_Y = 0.053900001570582390 BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_QUAD_SPAN = 0.028800001833587885
-- {time, value} keyframes, linear between (M2 track interpolation 1) — the file's own keys, -- at full precision. The three tracks keep DIFFERENT schedules and that is the whole feel: -- the card fades up while swelling to 1.2x over 133 ms, settles back to full size at -- 267 ms, then dwindles and fades *continuously* for the remaining 733 ms — while its -- position holds until the half second and only then falls. So it is already at ~0.69 size -- and ~0.68 alpha when it starts to move, and it is invisible by the time it lands. BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_ALPHA = { {0.000, 0.0}, {0.133, 1.0}, {0.267, 1.0}, {1.000, 0.0} } BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_SCALE = { {0.000, 1.0}, {0.133, 1.2000000476837158}, {0.267, 1.0}, {1.000, 0.01441549975425005} } -- Translation is per-AXIS: the card falls 51.4 px and drifts 13.3 px RIGHT, so one shared -- 0..1 "drop" curve (0887's shape) cannot express it — the old code had no horizontal term -- at all and moved the card the wrong way in x when it inferred one. BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_TRANS_X = { {0.000, 0.0}, {0.500, 0.0}, {1.000, 0.010394600220024586} } BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_TRANS_Y = { {0.000, 0.0}, {0.500, 0.0}, {1.000, -0.040167398750782013} }
-- Sample a {time, value} keyframe list at `t`, linear between keys, clamped at both ends -- (the M2 sampler's own shape for a CLAMP sequence). function BenillaItemPushAnim_Sample(track, t) local last = table.getn(track) if t <= track[1][1] then return track[1][2] end for i = 2, last do local key = track[i] if t <= key[1] then local prev = track[i - 1] local span = key[1] - prev[1] if span <= 0 then return key[2] end return prev[2] + (key[2] - prev[2]) * (t - prev[1]) / span end end return track[last][2] end
-- Place/size/fade the card for the current clock, from the model's own transform. -- -- The card's centre in MODEL space is `pivot + T(t) + S(t)*(quadCentre - pivot)`; times the -- projection constant that is its offset in layout units from the model origin, which is -- the widget rect's bottom-left corner. The rect's own BOTTOMRIGHT hangs off the button's, -- so the card is placed against the BUTTON'S BOTTOMRIGHT — never its centre — and the -- frame width is what converts between the two. -- -- On screen: a button-sized card appears with its bottom edge ~13.6 px ABOVE the button's -- top, pops to 1.2x and back while fading in, hangs there through the first half second, -- then falls down-and-right INTO the button, shrinking to a half-pixel point at its centre -- as it fades out. Reproduces the reference at t = 0, 0.133 and 1.0 to the hundredth of a -- pixel (`modelframe-implicit-size-law.md` §3's table). -- -- NOT modelled, deliberately, and both are named in the record: the reference's widget -- CLIPS the card to its own rect, which shaves 1.94 px off the right edge at the 1.2x peak -- **at 4:3 only** (16:10 and 16:9 clear it); and the widget clears the depth buffer inside -- that 124.72-tall rect every paint. benilla draws this as a Texture, not a Model, so it -- inherits neither — reproducing an aspect-conditional sliver would be hard-coding a -- rendering artefact rather than modelling the mechanism that causes it. function BenillaItemPushAnim_Paint(anim) local t = anim.elapsed local k = BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_PX_PER_UNIT local scale = BenillaItemPushAnim_Sample(BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_SCALE, t) local size = BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_QUAD_SPAN * scale * k local cx = (BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_PIVOT_X + BenillaItemPushAnim_Sample(BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_TRANS_X, t) + scale * (BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_QUAD_X - BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_PIVOT_X)) * k local cy = (BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_PIVOT_Y + BenillaItemPushAnim_Sample(BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_TRANS_Y, t) + scale * (BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_QUAD_Y - BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_PIVOT_Y)) * k anim:SetWidth(size) anim:SetHeight(size) anim:SetPoint("CENTER", anim:GetParent(), "BOTTOMRIGHT", anim.anchorX - BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_FRAME_W + cx, cy) anim:SetAlpha(BenillaItemPushAnim_Sample(BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_ALPHA, t)) end
-- ref ItemAnim_OnLoad (l.68-70): the card listens for ITEM_PUSH and nothing else. It is -- authored hidden, so it costs no OnUpdate until a push shows it (events reach hidden -- frames; OnUpdate does not — the reference's own split). function BenillaItemPushAnim_OnLoad(anim, containerId, anchorX) anim.containerId = containerId -- The widget's own offset from the button's BOTTOMRIGHT: -10 for the five bag buttons, -- flush 0 for the keyring (the ref's two different anchors — see the constant block). anim.anchorX = anchorX or BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_ANCHOR_X anim.icon = anim.icon or getglobal(anim:GetName() .. "Icon") anim.elapsed = 0 anim:RegisterEvent("ITEM_PUSH") end
-- ref ItemAnim_OnEvent (l.72-80): `if this:GetParent():GetID() == arg1`, then -- ReplaceIconTexture(arg2) / SetSequence(0) / SetSequenceTime(0,0) / Show. A push into a bag -- with no button (a bank bag) matches nothing and animates nowhere, there and here. function BenillaItemPushAnim_OnEvent(anim) if arg1 ~= anim.containerId then return end anim.icon:SetTexture(arg2) anim.elapsed = 0 -- Seat the card above its button rather than at load: the bag bar's own level is set in -- the BUTTON's OnLoad (BenillaActionBarArt_SeatAbove), which the loader may run after -- this child exists. Re-deriving it per push is one call and can never read it stale. anim:SetFrameLevel(anim:GetParent():GetFrameLevel() + 1) BenillaItemPushAnim_Paint(anim) anim:Show() end
-- The CLAMP sequence's end is the ref's OnAnimFinished → this:Hide() (l.92-94). function BenillaItemPushAnim_OnUpdate(anim, elapsed) anim.elapsed = anim.elapsed + (elapsed or 0) if anim.elapsed >= BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_DURATION then anim:Hide() return end BenillaItemPushAnim_Paint(anim) end
-- The six buttons and the offset each one's card hangs at, read off the reference's own -- anchors: BOTTOMRIGHT -10 for the five bag buttons (`BagSlotButtonTemplate` l.19-27 and -- `MainMenuBarBackpackButton` l.69-77), flush 0 for the keyring (l.152-160). BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_BUTTONS = { { "MainMenuBarBackpackButton", -10 }, { "CharacterBag0Slot", -10 }, { "CharacterBag1Slot", -10 }, { "CharacterBag2Slot", -10 }, { "CharacterBag3Slot", -10 }, { "KeyRingButton", 0 }, }
-- Build one button's card. Authored hidden, so it costs no OnUpdate until a push shows it -- — the reference's own split (events reach hidden frames, OnUpdate does not). -- -- Named `$parentBenillaItemPush` rather than `$parentItemAnim`: the reference's Model -- already owns that name on every one of these buttons, and an addon that reaches for it -- must find the reference's frame, not ours. function BenillaItemPushAnim_Attach(button, anchorX) local anim = CreateFrame("Frame", button:GetName() .. "BenillaItemPush", button) anim:Hide() anim:SetWidth(36) anim:SetHeight(36) anim:SetPoint("CENTER", button, "CENTER", 0, 0) anim.icon = anim:CreateTexture(anim:GetName() .. "Icon", "OVERLAY") anim.icon:SetAllPoints(anim) BenillaItemPushAnim_OnLoad(anim, button:GetID(), anchorX) anim:SetScript("OnEvent", function() BenillaItemPushAnim_OnEvent(this) end) anim:SetScript("OnUpdate", function() BenillaItemPushAnim_OnUpdate(this, arg1) end) return anim end
-- At load, because the bar is entry 48 and this file is entry 50 — every button exists and -- has run its own OnLoad, so `GetID()` is already the reference's. A button that is absent -- (a harness that loaded no bar) is skipped rather than raising: the card is a flourish, -- and a missing bar is not this file's error to report. for _, entry in ipairs(BENILLA_ITEM_PUSH_BUTTONS) do local button = getglobal(entry[1]) if button then BenillaItemPushAnim_Attach(button, entry[2]) end end
